definition_en: the part of the day between noon and evening
core_image: 正午的日影慢慢拉长，一天走过后半程
scene: 午后的教室空了大半，窗外的光斜斜照进来。In the quiet afternoon, the classroom emptied and the light came in sideways.
sceneCN: 这里 afternoon 是「午后时段」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们在温暖的午后走路回家。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -s 构成，义为「每天下午」（美式口语）
由 mid- 与本词复合，义为「午后中间时段」

senses.title: The part of the day after noon
senses.definition: the part of the day from noon until evening
senses.definitionCN: 正午到傍晚之间的时段
senses.example: We walked home in the warm afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在温暖的午后走路回家。
senses.why: Afternoon is simply after plus noon, so the word names the hours that follow the middle of the day.
senses.whyCN: afternoon 就是 after 加 noon，字面意思是「正午之后」，所以它指正午到傍晚的那段时间。

senses.title: The later half of a life or period
senses.definition: the later stage of a life or of a period, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻人生、事业或某个时代的后半段
senses.example: He called middle age the afternoon of life.
senses.exampleCN: 他把中年称作人生的午后。
senses.why: A day runs from morning through noon to dusk, and a life runs from youth through middle age to old age, so afternoon can stand for the later half.
senses.whyCN: 一天从早晨经正午走向黄昏，人的一生也从青年经中年走向老年，两者节奏相似，于是 afternoon 可以比喻后半段。

intro.en: The history of afternoon is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: afternoon 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: After and noon were joined to name the hours past midday.
items.cn: after 与 noon 组合起来，命名正午之后的时段。

items.en: Nōn first meant the ninth hour of the day, about three in the afternoon.
items.cn: 古英语 nōn 最初指一天中的第九时，约下午三点。

items.en: The church borrowed Latin nona hora, the ninth hour of prayer.
items.cn: 教会借用了拉丁语 nona hora，即第九时祈祷。

items.en: By the fourteenth century noon had moved to twelve o'clock, and afternoon followed it.
items.cn: 到十四世纪 noon 移到十二点，afternoon 也随之移动。

items.en: The compound now covers the whole stretch from midday to evening.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个复合词覆盖从正午到傍晚的整段时间。

core_image: 一面写着「我」的小牌，插在当下这一刻的位置上
scene: 清晨的门口，孩子背着书包正要出发。I am ready for school, said the boy at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 am 是「第一人称现在式」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我准备好了。

senses.title: The first-person singular of be
senses.definition: the form of be used with I in the present tense
senses.definitionCN: be 动词在第一人称单数现在时的形式，意为「我是」
senses.example: I am a student.
senses.why: English marks person on be: I takes am, while you and they take are, so am exists to pair with the pronoun I.
senses.whyCN: 英语的 be 动词按人称变形：I 后面用 am，you 和 they 后面用 are，am 就是专门跟「我」搭配的形式。

senses.title: To be somewhere or in some state
senses.definition: used with I to say where someone is or how someone feels
senses.definitionCN: 与 I 连用，说明「我」在何处或处于什么状态
senses.example: I am at home now.
senses.why: The same am does not always join I to a name; before a place or an adjective it reports location or condition instead.
senses.whyCN: am 不一定总把「我」和身份连起来；后面接地点或形容词时，它说的是「我在哪里」或「我怎么样」。

items.en: *h₁es- is reconstructed as the root of 'to be', with first-person *h₁ésmi.
items.cn: 原始印欧语 *h₁es- 被重构为「是」的词根，第一人称作 *h₁ésmi。

items.en: Germanic *immi became Old English eom, the first-person present of wesan.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *immi 演变为古英语 eom，即 wesan 的第一人称现在式。

items.en: Eom carried a long vowel and weakened to am in unstressed positions.
items.cn: 古英语 eom 原带长元音，在非重读位置上弱化为 am。

items.en: Am settled as the first-person form while be served the infinitive.
items.cn: 中古英语时期 am 固定为第一人称形式，be 则承担不定式。

items.en: Am, is and are are now treated as one paradigm supplied by different old verbs.
items.cn: 现代语法把 am、is、are 视为同一个 paradigm，由不同的古动词补足。

senses.title: Joining two things of the same kind
senses.definition: used to join two words, phrases or clauses of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 连接同类的词、短语或句子，表示并列
senses.example: Tom and I are friends.
senses.why: Its oldest job is to put two equal things side by side, as in bread and butter, so the first sense is plain addition.
senses.whyCN: and 最早的功能就是把两个对等的事物并排放，比如 bread and butter，所以第一层意思就是单纯的并列。

senses.title: Linking one action to the next
senses.definition: used to connect actions that follow one another
senses.definitionCN: 连接先后发生的动作，表示承接
senses.example: She sat down and cried.
senses.why: When the two joined parts are events rather than things, the order of the sentence becomes a sequence in time.
senses.whyCN: 当被连接的两部分不是事物而是事件时，句子的先后顺序自然变成时间上的先后，and 就有了「然后」的意思。

senses.title: The word between hundreds and smaller numbers
senses.definition: used between hundreds and the smaller number that follows
senses.definitionCN: 在百位与后面的十位或个位之间起连接作用
senses.example: One hundred and five people came.
senses.why: British English reads 105 as one hundred and five, so and fills the gap between the hundred and the units.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语把 105 读作 one hundred and five，and 在这里填补百位与个位之间的空档。

definition_en: the round fruit of a tree of the rose family, usually red or green
core_image: 餐桌上滚圆的红果，皮上还带着一层薄薄的亮
scene: 午后的餐桌上摆着刚洗好的水果，孩子伸手挑了一个。The child picked the red apple and bit into it.
sceneCN: 这里 apple 是「圆形果实」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她午饭后吃了一个苹果。

senses.title: The round fruit of the apple tree
senses.definition: a round fruit with red, green or yellow skin and firm flesh
senses.definitionCN: 一种圆形果实，果皮红、绿或黄，果肉紧实
senses.example: She ate an apple after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 她午饭后吃了一个苹果。
senses.why: Apple comes straight from Old English æppel, which named this common fruit, so the fruit is the word's original sense.
senses.whyCN: apple 直接继承古英语 æppel，最初就指这种常见果实，所以「苹果」是它最本源的意思。

senses.title: The tree that bears apples
senses.definition: the tree on which apples grow
senses.definitionCN: 结出苹果的果树
senses.example: The apple in the yard is full of red fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 院子里的苹果树挂满了红果。
senses.why: Old English also used æppel for the tree, and growers still say an apple when they mean the tree in an orchard.
senses.whyCN: 古英语里 æppel 也能指树，园艺行话至今仍用 an apple 表示果园里的「一棵苹果树」。

intro.cn: apple 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Germanic *aplaz is the reconstructed ancestor of English apple and German Apfel.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *aplaz 是英语 apple 与德语 Apfel 的重构祖先。

items.en: Old English æppel meant the fruit and could also mean fruit in general.
items.cn: 古英语 æppel 指这种果实，也曾泛指水果。

items.en: The spelling settled as apple while the broad sense narrowed.
items.cn: 中古英语时期拼写固定为 apple，宽泛词义收窄。

items.en: Compounds keep the word in daily food language.
items.cn: 复合词让这个词留在日常饮食语言里。

senses.title: The limb between shoulder and hand
senses.definition: either of the two long parts of the body between the shoulder and the hand
senses.definitionCN: 人体肩部与手之间的上肢
senses.example: He raised his arm to wave.
senses.why: Arm in this sense is a native English word from Old English earm, and it names the limb itself.
senses.whyCN: 表示「手臂」的 arm 是古英语 earm 传下来的本族词，指的就是这条肢体本身。

senses.title: The side of a chair that holds your arm
senses.definition: the part of a chair that supports your arm
senses.definitionCN: 椅子两侧支撑手臂的部分
senses.example: She leaned on the arm of the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠在这把椅子的扶手上。
senses.why: A chair's side piece holds your arm, so speakers simply transferred the body-part name to the furniture.
senses.whyCN: 椅子两侧托住手臂的部件，人们就把身体部位的名字直接挪用到家具上。

senses.title: Weapons, especially in the plural
senses.definition: weapons, especially in the plural form arms
senses.definitionCN: 武器，常用复数 arms
senses.example: The soldiers laid down their arms.
senses.why: This sense does not come from the limb at all: it descends from Latin arma, meaning tools of war, and only shares the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项和肢体无关：它来自拉丁语 arma「战争工具」，只是拼写与「手臂」相同。

items.en: *h₂erm- or *h₂ar- is reconstructed for 'arm, shoulder'; the exact shape is source uncertain.
items.cn: 「臂、肩」一般重构为 *h₂erm- 或 *h₂ar-，确切形式来源不确定。

items.en: Germanic *armaz is the ancestor of English arm and German Arm.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *armaz 是英语 arm 与德语 Arm 的祖先。

items.en: Old English earm covered the limb and the sleeve of a garment.
items.cn: 古英语 earm 既指肢体，也指衣服的袖子。

items.en: The limb sense stayed central while figurative parts developed later.
items.cn: 肢体义仍是中心，比喻性的部件义随后发展。

items.en: The weapon plural arms comes separately from Latin arma.
items.cn: 表示武器的复数 arms 另从拉丁语 arma 而来。

definition_zh: 在（某地点或某时刻）；在……方面
definition_en: a preposition marking a point in place or time, or the target of an action
core_image: 地图上的一个小圆点，标出事情发生的那一处
scene: 放学后的校门口，家长三三两两站着等孩子。The parents waited at the school gate for their children.
sceneCN: 这里 at 是「地点上的点」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们在门口见面。

derivatives.zh: 由 at 与 home 合成，义为「在家进行的」
由 at 与 risk 合成，义为「处于风险中的」

senses.title: A point in place
senses.definition: in or near a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 在某个地点或某个位置
senses.example: She is at the door.
senses.why: At began as a word for contact or position, and English uses it for a point on a map or a spot in a room.
senses.whyCN: at 最初表示接触或位置，英语用它指出地图上的一个点或房间里的一个位置。

senses.title: A point in time
senses.definition: at a particular point in time
senses.definitionCN: 在某个具体的时刻
senses.example: We meet at six.
senses.why: The same idea of a point works for the clock: six o'clock is a single point on the day's line.
senses.whyCN: 「一个点」的概念也适用于钟点：六点正是时间线上单独的一点。

senses.title: The target of a look or action
senses.definition: toward or in the direction of something
senses.definitionCN: 朝向某个对象或目标
senses.example: She looked at the map.
senses.why: When the point is not a place but an object of attention, at marks what the eyes or mind aim toward.
senses.whyCN: 当这个「点」不是地点而是注意的对象时，at 标记目光或心思所朝向的东西。

senses.title: A level, rate or state
senses.definition: used before a state, level or speed
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出状态、水平或速度
senses.example: The car ran at high speed.
senses.why: A measurement such as speed or price is treated as a point on a scale, so at introduces the level.
senses.whyCN: 速度、价格这类数值被看作刻度上的一个点，所以用 at 引出这个水平。

intro.en: The history of at is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: at 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: At is recorded as æt, meaning 'at, near, in'.
items.cn: at 在古英语中写作 æt，意为「在、靠近」。

items.en: A Germanic preposition *at underlies the English, German and Gothic forms.
items.cn: 日耳曼介词 *at 是英语、德语与哥特语诸形式的底层。

items.en: It is generally connected with a root meaning 'near, by'; the deeper source is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为与表示「靠近」的词根有关；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English used æt with the dative, whose endings have since disappeared.
items.cn: 古英语 æt 支配与格，其词尾后来消失。

items.en: Bare at survives and multiplies its fixed phrases.
items.cn: 光杆 at 保留下来，并大量扩展固定短语。

definition_zh: 八月；威严的；令人敬畏的
definition_en: the eighth month of the year, and as an adjective, majestic and inspiring awe
core_image: 盛夏将尽时，一队披着长袍的祭司在石阶上缓缓走过
scene: 夏末的庭院里，石榴已经红透，热气还没有散。The family always visits the lake in August.
sceneCN: 这里 august 是「第八个月」（第 01 个义项）；句意是学校八月开学。

pos.zh: 形容词：威严的、令人敬畏的

derivatives.zh: 由 August 加 -an 构成，义为「奥古斯都时代的」
由形容词 august 加 -ly 构成，义为「威严地」

senses.title: The eighth month of the year
senses.definition: the eighth month of the year
senses.definitionCN: 一年中的第八个月
senses.example: School begins in August.
senses.why: The month is named after Augustus Caesar, so August began as a proper name and then became the ordinary word for the eighth month.
senses.whyCN: 这个月以罗马皇帝奥古斯都命名，August 先作专名，后来才变成「八月」的普通说法。

senses.title: Grand and worthy of respect
senses.definition: grand and impressive, inspiring respect
senses.definitionCN: 庄严气派、令人肃然起敬的
senses.example: The old hall had an august presence.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古老的大厅有一种威严的气派。
senses.why: The adjective august comes from the same Latin word meaning consecrated or majestic, and it describes people or things that inspire reverence.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 august 来自同一个拉丁词，意为「神圣、庄严」，用来形容令人肃然起敬的人或物。

intro.en: The history of august is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: august 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: The title augustus meant 'consecrated, revered'.
items.cn: 称号 augustus 意为「神圣的、受尊崇的」。

items.en: Augustus derives from augere, 'to increase', with a religious charge of growth.
items.cn: Augustus 来自 augere「增加」，带增长与祝福的宗教意味。

items.en: The month Sextilis was renamed Augustus in honour of the emperor.
items.cn: 罗马历中原名 Sextilis 的月份为纪念皇帝改称 Augustus。

items.en: English took the month name through the church calendar as August.
items.cn: 英语经由教会历法吸收这个月名，作 August。

items.en: The adjective august 'majestic' entered separately from the same Latin title.
items.cn: 表示「威严」的形容词从同一拉丁称号另路进入英语。

definition_en: a container made of flexible material with an opening at the top
core_image: 一块软布四角收拢，东西都落进同一个兜里
scene: 早市上摊主把新摘的豆角倒进布袋，秤杆还挂着。The seller filled a bag with beans and handed it over.
sceneCN: 这里 bag 是「有开口的容器」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她用布袋子装米。

derivatives.zh: 由 bag 加 -ful 构成，义为「一袋之量」
由 bag 加 -y 构成，义为「宽松鼓起的」
经由法语来自同一 bag 词，义为「行李」

senses.title: A container open at the top
senses.definition: a container made of paper, cloth or plastic, open at the top
senses.definitionCN: 用纸、布或塑料制成、上端开口的容器
senses.example: She carried the fruit in a paper bag.
senses.exampleCN: 她把水果装在一个纸袋里。
senses.why: Bag probably comes from Old Norse baggi, a pack or bundle, so the container is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: bag 很可能来自古诺斯语 baggi「包裹、一捆」，所以「容器」是最早的意思。

senses.title: The amount a bag holds
senses.definition: the amount that a bag holds
senses.definitionCN: 一只袋子所能装下的分量
senses.example: He bought a bag of rice.
senses.why: Once a container is familiar, its name can measure what fills it, so a bag of rice means the quantity inside one bag.
senses.whyCN: 容器一旦常见，它的名字就能计量所装的东西，a bag of rice 指一袋能装下的量。

senses.title: The bag a person carries daily
senses.definition: a handbag or a school bag carried every day
senses.definitionCN: 日常随身携带的手提包或书包
senses.example: She put her keys in her bag.
senses.why: In everyday British English bag often shortens handbag or school bag, the bag a person carries all day.
senses.whyCN: 在日常英式英语里，bag 常用来简称 handbag 或 school bag，也就是随身携带的那只包。

intro.en: The history of bag is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: bag 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Bag appears in Middle English, probably from Old Norse baggi; the earlier source is uncertain.
items.cn: bag 见于中古英语，可能来自古诺斯语 baggi；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old Norse baggi meant a bundle or pack, spread by Norse trade.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 baggi 指一捆或一包，随北欧贸易传播。

items.en: No reliable Indo-European root is agreed; the word may be a loan.
items.cn: 没有公认的可靠印欧词根；这个词可能是借词。

items.en: The noun widened from a pack to handbags and luggage.
items.cn: 现代英语中名词从包裹扩展到提包与行李。

items.en: The verb grew in the nineteenth century and later took the sense of securing.
items.cn: 动词用法在十九世纪发展起来，后来又产生「抢先占取」义。

definition_en: a round object used in games, or any rounded mass
core_image: 一只圆球在地上滚，碰到什么就弹向另一边
scene: 操场边的孩子把圆的东西一脚踢出去，另一个追着跑。The boy chased the ball across the playground.
sceneCN: 这里 ball 是「游戏用的球」（第 01 个义项）；句意是孩子们踢球。

derivatives.zh: 由 ball 加增扩后缀 -oon 构成，义为「气球」
由 ball 与 game 复合，义为「球赛」
由 ball 与 boy 复合，义为「球童」

senses.title: A round object used in games
senses.definition: a round object that is thrown, kicked or hit in games
senses.definitionCN: 游戏中用来投、踢或击打的圆形物体
senses.example: The boy kicked the ball.
senses.why: Ball came from Old Norse böllr, meaning a round object, and the plaything is its central sense.
senses.whyCN: ball 来自古诺斯语 böllr「圆形物」，玩具球就是它最核心的意思。

senses.title: A game played with a ball
senses.definition: a game in which a ball is used
senses.definitionCN: 使用球的运动或比赛
senses.example: They played ball after school.
senses.why: Because the ball is the thing the game revolves around, playing ball came to name the game itself.
senses.whyCN: 球是整场游戏围绕的东西，所以 play ball 逐渐用来指这项运动本身。

senses.title: A formal social dance
senses.definition: a formal party with dancing
senses.definitionCN: 伴有跳舞的正式社交聚会
senses.example: She wore a long dress to the ball.
senses.why: This sense has a different origin: it comes from French bal, a dance, and only later fell together in spelling with the plaything.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来源不同：它来自法语 bal「舞会」，后来才和表示球的 ball 拼成同一个词。

senses.title: A rounded mass of something soft
senses.definition: something soft wound or pressed into a round shape
senses.definitionCN: 柔软的东西卷成或压成的圆团
senses.example: He rolled the wool into a ball.
senses.why: Anything wound into a round mass looks like a ball, so the shape, not the game, gave this fourth sense.
senses.whyCN: 任何卷成圆团的东西都像球，所以这层意思来自形状，而不是来自游戏。

items.en: German Ball and Dutch bal point to a Germanic word for something round.
items.cn: 德语 Ball 与荷兰语 bal 指向一个表示「圆」的日耳曼词。

items.en: A link with a root meaning 'to swell' is often suggested but remains source uncertain.

items.en: The dance sense came separately through French bal.
items.cn: 舞会义另经法语 bal 进入英语。

definition_en: a long curved fruit with soft yellow flesh and a thick skin
core_image: 一串弯月似的黄果挂在宽叶间，皮一剥就露出白肉
scene: 南方的果园里，宽大的叶子遮住阳光，一串黄果垂得很低。The farmer cut a ripe banana from the bunch.
sceneCN: 这里 banana 是「香蕉果实」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她早餐剥了一根香蕉。

derivatives.zh: 由 banana 与 bread 复合，义为「香蕉面包」
由 banana 与 skin 复合，义为「香蕉皮」

senses.title: The long yellow fruit
senses.definition: a long curved fruit with soft yellow flesh and a thick skin
senses.definitionCN: 细长弯曲、果肉柔软、外皮厚实的黄色果实
senses.example: She peeled a banana for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 她早餐时剥了一根香蕉。
senses.why: Banana came into English through Spanish and Portuguese from a West African name for the fruit, so the fruit is the word's first sense.
senses.whyCN: banana 经西班牙语和葡萄牙语进入英语，源头是西非对这种果实的称呼，所以「果实」是它最早的意思。

senses.title: The tropical plant that bears bananas
senses.definition: the tall tropical plant on which bananas grow
senses.definitionCN: 结出香蕉的高大热带植物
senses.example: The banana grows best in hot, wet countries.
senses.exampleCN: 香蕉树在炎热潮湿的国家长得最好。
senses.why: Growers use the same name for the plant and its fruit, just as English does with apple and orange.
senses.whyCN: 种植者用同一个名称指果树和果实，英语里的 apple、orange 也是这样。

intro.en: The history of banana is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: banana 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: The word is usually traced to a West African language, often Wolof banaana; the exact source is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词通常追溯到西非语言，多认为来自沃洛夫语 banaana；确切来源不确定。

items.en: Portuguese and Spanish traders carried banana into European languages.
items.cn: 葡萄牙与西班牙商人把 banana 带入欧洲语言。

items.en: English records the fruit name from the late sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语自十六世纪末记录这一果实名称。

items.en: Plantations and shipping spread the fruit and the word together.
items.cn: 种植园与航运把果实和词一起传开。

items.en: Banana now covers the fruit, the plant and foods made from it.
items.cn: 现代英语中 banana 覆盖果实、植株与相关食品。

definition_en: very pleasing to the senses or to the mind
core_image: 夕阳穿过窗子，把整间屋子的轮廓都镀上一层暖金
scene: 雨停了，山谷里的水面把云影完整地映出来。The valley looked beautiful after the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 beautiful 是「外貌美丽」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她穿了一条美丽的裙子。

pos.zh: 形容词：美丽的、美好的、出色的

derivatives.zh: 由 beautiful 加 -ly 构成，义为「美丽地」
beautiful 所由构成的名词，义为「美」
由 beautiful 加 -ness 构成，义为「美丽」

senses.title: Pleasing to look at or hear
senses.definition: very pleasing to the eyes or ears
senses.definitionCN: 看起来或听起来非常悦目悦耳的
senses.example: The garden looks beautiful in spring.
senses.why: Beautiful is beauty plus the suffix -ful, so its first job is to describe something full of beauty, whether a face, a view or a song.
senses.whyCN: beautiful 是 beauty 加后缀 -ful，最初的意思就是「充满美的」，所以首先用来形容容貌、景色或歌声。

senses.title: Excellent or very well done
senses.definition: very good or impressive, used in praise
senses.definitionCN: 非常好、令人赞叹，用于称赞
senses.example: What a beautiful goal!
senses.why: Speakers borrowed the word from looks to performance: a beautiful goal or a beautiful pass is not pretty but perfectly executed.
senses.whyCN: 说话的人把这个词从「外表」挪到「表现」：a beautiful goal 或 a beautiful pass 不是好看，而是完成得极为漂亮。

intro.en: The history of beautiful is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: beautiful 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Latin bellus meant 'pretty, fine', a small-scale word of praise.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bellus 意为「好看、精致」，是一个程度较轻的赞美词。

items.en: Old French beau and belle carried the Latin word into French.
items.cn: 古法语 beau 与 belle 把这一拉丁词带入法语。

items.en: Middle English borrowed beaute, the noun for beauty.
items.cn: 中古英语借入名词 beaute，即「美」。

items.en: Beautiful was formed in English from beauty plus the suffix -ful.
items.cn: beautiful 是在英语中用 beauty 加后缀 -ful 构成的。

items.en: The adjective widened from looks to sound, character and skill.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个形容词从外貌扩展到声音、品格与技艺。

definition_en: a piece of furniture that people sleep on, or a flat base for something
core_image: 一张铺着厚被的木床，夜里把整天的疲惫都接住
scene: 夜深了，屋里的灯熄了，窗外的雨声盖过了脚步。The child climbed into bed and fell asleep at once.
sceneCN: 这里 bed 是「睡觉的家具」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她早饭前整理了床铺。

collocations.zh: 提供住宿与早餐的旅店

derivatives.zh: 由 bed 加 -ing 构成，义为「床上用品」
由 bed 与 room 复合，义为「卧室」
由 bed 与 time 复合，义为「就寝时间」

senses.title: The furniture people sleep on
senses.definition: a piece of furniture with a mattress that people sleep on
senses.definitionCN: 供人睡觉的家具，上面铺有床垫
senses.example: The cat slept under the bed.
senses.why: Bed comes from a Germanic word for a sleeping place, and the furniture sense is the one children meet first.
senses.whyCN: bed 来自日耳曼语中表示「睡觉之处」的词，而「家具床」是孩子最先接触的意思。

senses.title: The bottom of a river or the sea
senses.definition: the ground beneath a river, lake or sea
senses.definitionCN: 河流、湖泊或海洋底部的地面
senses.example: The river bed was dry in summer.
senses.why: A river lies on its bed the way a sleeper lies on a bed, so the flat ground under water took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 河水躺在河床上，就像人躺在床里，于是水下那片平坦的地面也借用了 bed 这个名字。

senses.title: A plot of soil for plants
senses.definition: a piece of ground prepared for growing flowers or vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 整理好用来种花或种菜的土块
senses.example: She planted roses in the flower bed.
senses.why: A garden bed is a raised strip of prepared soil, shaped like a long low bed, which is why gardeners use the word.
senses.whyCN: 花坛是一条整理好、微微隆起的土畦，形状像一张长而低的床，园丁因此沿用 bed 这个词。

intro.en: The history of bed is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: bed 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: A root *bʰedʰ- meaning 'to dig' is often reconstructed; the link is source uncertain.
items.cn: 常重构出一个表示「挖」的词根 *bʰedʰ-；这一关联来源不确定。

items.en: Germanic *badją gave Old English bedd and German Bett.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *badją 产生古英语 bedd 与德语 Bett。

items.en: Bedd meant a sleeping place and also a plot of ground.
items.cn: 古英语 bedd 既指睡处，也指一块土地。

items.en: The furniture sense became central while the ground sense survived in compounds.
items.cn: 中古英语时期家具义成为中心，地面义在复合词中留存。

items.en: River bed, flower bed and machine bed extend the flat-base image.
items.cn: 河床、花坛与机器底座都延伸了「平底」这一形象。

definition_zh: 大的；重要的；年长的；慷慨的
definition_en: large in size, importance or degree
core_image: 一只手掌张开，比划出抱不住那么大的一团
scene: 搬家的卡车停在巷口，纸箱堆得比门还高。They moved the big table into the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 big 是「体积大」（第 01 个义项）；句意是一个大箱子堵住了门。

pos.zh: 形容词：大的、重要的、年长的

derivatives.zh: 由 big 加比较级后缀 -er 构成，义为「更大的」
由 big 加最高级后缀 -est 构成，义为「最大的」
由 big 加 -ness 构成，义为「巨大」

senses.title: Large in size
senses.definition: large in size or amount
senses.definitionCN: 体积或数量大的
senses.example: The box is too big for the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 这个箱子太大，放不进架子。
senses.why: Big is a native word whose oldest meaning is simply large in size, and that physical sense remains the clearest one.
senses.whyCN: big 是本族词，最早的意思就是体积大，这个物理意义至今最清楚。

senses.title: Important or serious
senses.definition: important or serious in effect
senses.definitionCN: 影响重大或严重的
senses.example: Learning to swim was a big step for him.
senses.exampleCN: 学会游泳对他来说是重要的一步。
senses.why: Something physically large takes more space and attention, so big easily shifts from size to importance.
senses.whyCN: 体积大的东西占据更多空间、也更受注意，所以 big 很容易从「尺寸」转向「重要性」。

senses.title: Older, of a sibling
senses.definition: older, used of a brother or sister
senses.definitionCN: 用于兄弟姐妹时表示年龄更大
senses.example: My big brother taught me to ride a bike.
senses.why: Children judge age by height and size, so the older sibling is naturally the big one in family speech.
senses.whyCN: 孩子常按身高和体型判断年龄，所以在家庭用语里，年长的兄弟姐妹自然就是 big 的那一个。

intro.en: The history of big is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: big 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Big appears in northern English from about the fourteenth century; its origin is uncertain.
items.cn: big 约自十四世纪见于英格兰北部；来源不确定。

items.en: A link with a Scandinavian word for 'big, bulky' has been suggested but is not settled.
items.cn: 有人提出它与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「大而笨重」的词有关，但未成定论。

items.en: The word spread south and replaced older terms for large size.
items.cn: 这个词向南传播，取代了较早表示「大」的说法。

items.en: Its range widened from size to importance and generosity.
items.cn: 现代英语中它的范围从尺寸扩展到重要性与宽厚。

items.en: Big survives in many fixed phrases such as big deal and big heart.
items.cn: big 保留在 big deal、big heart 等大量固定短语中。

definition_en: a two-wheeled vehicle moved by pedals, or to ride one
core_image: 两个轮子一条线，脚一蹬就带着人往前滑
scene: 清晨的巷子里，铃声一路响过去，车轮压过浅浅的水洼。He rode his bike to school along the narrow lane.
sceneCN: 这里 bike 是「自行车」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她买了一辆新自行车。

derivatives.zh: 由 bike 加 -er 构成，义为「骑手」
由 bike 加 -ing 构成，义为「骑行活动」

senses.title: A two-wheeled bicycle
senses.definition: a vehicle with two wheels that a person moves by pedalling
senses.definitionCN: 靠人踩踏板驱动的两轮交通工具
senses.example: He rides his bike to school.
senses.why: Bike is a short form of bicycle, which joins bi- meaning two with the Greek root for wheel, so the two wheels are built into the name.
senses.whyCN: bike 是 bicycle 的缩略形式，bicycle 由表示「二」的 bi- 和希腊语「轮」的词根组成，名称里就写着两个轮子。

senses.title: To ride a bicycle
senses.definition: to travel by bicycle
senses.definitionCN: 骑自行车出行
senses.example: She biked along the river.
senses.why: English often turns a vehicle noun into a verb with no change of form, so the thing you ride became the act of riding it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把交通工具的名词直接当动词用，词形不变，于是「你骑的那辆车」就变成了「骑」这个动作。

intro.en: The history of bike is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: bike 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Bike is a nineteenth-century shortening of bicycle.
items.cn: bike 是十九世纪对 bicycle 的缩略。

items.en: Bicycle was coined in French from Latin bi- 'two' and Greek kyklos 'wheel'.
items.cn: bicycle 在法语中用拉丁语 bi-「二」与希腊语 kyklos「轮」造出。

items.en: The Greek word for wheel also gives cycle and cyclone.
items.cn: 希腊语「轮」还给出 cycle 与 cyclone。

items.en: The short form became the everyday word in speech.
items.cn: 缩略形式成为口语中的日常说法。

items.en: Bike later covered motorcycles and exercise machines.
items.cn: bike 后来也覆盖摩托车与健身器械。

definition_zh: 黑色的；黑暗的；不加奶的；黑人的
definition_en: of the darkest colour, absorbing light rather than reflecting it
core_image: 夜里没有月亮的角落，光一进去就被吸得干干净净
scene: 停电后的走廊里，连台阶的边都看不清。The whole corridor went black when the power failed.
sceneCN: 这里 black 是「黑色」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她把门漆成黑色。

derivatives.zh: 由 black 加 -en 构成，义为「使变黑」
由 black 加 -ness 构成，义为「黑色、黑暗」
由 black 与 bird 复合，义为「黑鸟」

senses.title: The darkest colour
senses.definition: of the darkest colour, absorbing light rather than reflecting it
senses.definitionCN: 颜色最深的，吸收光线而不反射
senses.example: She wore a black coat.
senses.why: Black comes from Old English blæc, which named the colour of soot and night, so the colour is the word's base sense.
senses.whyCN: black 来自古英语 blæc，指烟灰与夜色那种颜色，所以「黑色」是它最基础的意思。

senses.title: Without light
senses.definition: dark, with no light
senses.definitionCN: 没有光线的、漆黑的
senses.example: The night was black and silent.
senses.why: A surface with no light reaching it looks black, so the colour word also describes darkness itself.
senses.whyCN: 没有光线照到的表面看起来就是黑的，所以这个颜色词也用来形容黑暗本身。

senses.title: Coffee without milk
senses.definition: served without milk or cream, of coffee
senses.definitionCN: 咖啡不加牛奶或奶油
senses.example: He drinks black coffee.
senses.why: Black coffee looks almost black in the cup, and the colour word became a fixed way to order it without milk.
senses.whyCN: 不加奶的咖啡在杯里近乎黑色，颜色词就这样固定成了「不加奶」的点单说法。

intro.en: The history of black is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: black 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Old English blæc meant black and also dark or gloomy.
items.cn: 古英语 blæc 既指黑色，也指昏暗阴郁。

items.en: Germanic *blakaz is the reconstructed source, related to words for burning.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *blakaz 是重构来源，与表示「燃烧」的词相关。

items.en: A link with a root for 'to burn, shine' is suggested; the exact history is source uncertain.
items.cn: 有人提出它与表示「燃烧、发光」的词根有关；确切历史来源不确定。

items.en: The colour sense dominated while figurative senses grew alongside.
items.cn: 中古英语时期颜色义占主导，比喻义同时生长。

items.en: Black covers coffee, markets, moods and communities.
items.cn: 现代英语中 black 覆盖咖啡、市场、情绪与群体。

definition_zh: 蓝色的；忧郁的；色情的（口语）
definition_en: of the colour of a clear sky, and in informal use, sad
core_image: 晴空最干净的那一块颜色，抬头就能看见
scene: 正午的海面很静，远处的颜色从浅到深铺开来。The sky turned deep blue above the harbour.
sceneCN: 这里 blue 是「蓝色」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她穿了一件蓝色外套。

derivatives.zh: 由 blue 加 -ish 构成，义为「略带蓝色的」
由 blue 加 -ness 构成，义为「蓝色」
由 blue 与 bird 复合，义为「蓝鸲」

senses.title: The colour of a clear sky
senses.definition: of the colour of a clear sky or the sea
senses.definitionCN: 晴朗天空或海水那种颜色
senses.example: The sky is blue today.
senses.why: Blue entered English from French bleu, and its first task was to name the colour of sky and sea.
senses.whyCN: blue 从法语 bleu 进入英语，最初的任务就是命名天空与海水的颜色。

senses.title: Sad or low in spirits
senses.definition: sad or gloomy, in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示情绪低落、忧郁
senses.example: He felt blue after the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 收到那封信后他情绪低落。
senses.why: The sad sense grew from the old idea of blue devils, spirits that were said to bring gloom, so the colour became a mood.
senses.whyCN: 表示忧郁的义项来自旧的 blue devils 说法，据说这种幽灵会带来阴郁，于是颜色词变成了心情词。

senses.title: The sky or the open sea
senses.definition: the sky or the sea, as in the phrase the blue
senses.definitionCN: 诗歌或书面语中用 the blue 指天空或大海
senses.example: The blue of the sea amazed us.
senses.exampleCN: 大海的蔚蓝让我们惊叹。
senses.why: Writers name the whole by its colour, so the blue can stand for the sky or the sea without naming either object.
senses.whyCN: 作家用颜色代指整体，所以 the blue 不用点明对象，就能指天空或大海。

intro.en: The history of blue is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.

items.en: English took blue from Old French bleu in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪从古法语 bleu 借入 blue。

items.en: The French word goes back to a Frankish *blāu, a Germanic colour term.
items.cn: 法语词可追溯到法兰克语 *blāu，一个日耳曼颜色词。

items.en: The deeper origin is source uncertain; it may relate to words for pale or light.
items.cn: 更早来源不确定，可能与表示「浅、亮」的词有关。

items.en: Blue replaced the older English word blæwen.
items.cn: blue 取代了较早的英语词 blæwen。

items.en: The colour word also gave the informal sense of sadness.
items.cn: 这个颜色词还发展出口语中的「忧郁」义。

definition_en: a set of printed pages bound together, or to reserve something in advance
core_image: 一叠裁齐的纸被装订成册，翻开就是一整个装进去的世界
scene: 雨天的下午，孩子把脸贴近书页，一行一行往下读。The child read the book slowly by the window.
sceneCN: 这里 book 是「装订成册的书」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她翻到书的第十页。

derivatives.zh: 由 book 加 -ing 构成，义为「预订」
由 book 加指小后缀 -let 构成，义为「小册子」
由 book 加 -ish 构成，义为「爱读书的」

senses.title: A set of printed pages
senses.definition: a set of printed pages bound together for reading
senses.definitionCN: 装订在一起、供阅读的一叠印有文字的纸页
senses.example: He read a book about stars.
senses.exampleCN: 他读了一本关于星星的书。
senses.why: Book goes back to Old English bōc, a word tied to beech wood, because early writing boards were made of beech.
senses.whyCN: book 可追溯到古英语 bōc，与榉木有关，因为早期的书写板正是用榉木做的。

senses.title: To reserve in advance
senses.definition: to arrange to have a seat, room or service kept for you
senses.definitionCN: 提前安排保留座位、房间或服务
senses.example: I booked a table for two.
senses.why: Shopkeepers once wrote reservations into a book, so to book came to mean putting something down before you use it.
senses.whyCN: 商人过去把预订记进账簿，所以 to book 逐渐表示「提前把事情记下、留好」。

senses.title: A record of accounts or names
senses.definition: a set of records kept for accounts or names
senses.definitionCN: 记录账目或名单的本子
senses.example: Her name is in the account book.
senses.why: Before printed books, any bound record was a book, and businesses still keep their accounts in one.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷书出现之前，任何装订起来的记录都叫 book，商家至今仍把账记在账簿里。

intro.en: The history of book is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: book 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Old English bōc meant a written document or a book, and its plural was bēc.
items.cn: 古英语 bōc 指文书或书，复数为 bēc。

items.en: Germanic *bōks is linked by many scholars to beech, the wood once used for writing tablets.

items.en: The link with a root for beech is widely accepted but the deeper history is source uncertain.
items.cn: 与「山毛榉」词根的关联被广泛接受，但更深的历史来源不确定。

items.en: The plural changed to books, and the word covered bound volumes.
items.cn: 中古英语时期复数变为 books，词义覆盖装订成册的书。

items.en: Book also became a verb meaning to reserve or register.
items.cn: 现代英语中 book 又作动词，表示预订或登记。

definition_en: a male sibling, or a man united with others by a shared group or cause
core_image: 两个从小一起长大的男孩，肩并肩站在同一道门槛上
scene: 老屋的门槛上，两个男孩一起等着父亲从田里回来。Her brother waited with her at the old doorstep.
sceneCN: 这里 brother 是「兄弟」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我哥哥住在邻镇。

derivatives.zh: 由 brother 加 -ly 构成，义为「兄弟般的」
由 brother 加 -hood 构成，义为「兄弟情谊」
brother 的古老复数，义为「教友、同道」

senses.title: A male sibling
senses.definition: a boy or man who has the same parents as another person
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人有相同父母的男性
senses.example: My brother is two years older.
senses.why: Brother comes from Old English brōþor, the old Germanic word for a male sibling, and that family sense is the oldest.
senses.whyCN: brother 来自古英语 brōþor，是日耳曼语中表示男性兄弟姐妹的旧词，家庭义项最为古老。

senses.title: A fellow member or close friend
senses.definition: a man united with others by a shared group, trade or cause
senses.definitionCN: 因共同群体、职业或事业而联结的男性
senses.example: The brothers fought side by side.
senses.why: People in the same group feel the closeness of siblings, so brother extends from the family to comrades and fellow members.
senses.whyCN: 同一群体里的人会感到像兄弟姐妹般亲近，于是 brother 从家庭扩展到战友与同伴。

senses.title: A religious title for a monk
senses.definition: the title used for a monk or a male member of a religious order
senses.definitionCN: 对修士或男性修会成员的称呼
senses.example: Brother John led the prayer.
senses.why: Religious orders call members brothers because they live as one family, which turned the kinship word into a formal title.
senses.whyCN: 修会称成员为 brothers，因为他们像一家人共同生活，这个亲属词就这样变成了正式称谓。

intro.cn: brother 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: *bʰréh₂tēr is reconstructed for 'brother', one of the oldest kinship words.
items.cn: 「兄弟」一般重构为 *bʰréh₂tēr，是最古老的亲属词之一。

items.en: Germanic *brōþēr became Old English brōþor and German Bruder.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *brōþēr 演变为古英语 brōþor 与德语 Bruder。

items.en: Brōþor covered both the family sense and members of a guild or order.
items.cn: 古英语 brōþor 既指家庭兄弟，也指行会或修会的成员。

items.en: The vowel shortened and the plural became brothers alongside brethren.
items.cn: 中古英语时期元音变短，复数既有 brothers 又有 brethren。

items.en: Brother extends to comrades, monks and forms of address.
items.cn: 现代英语中 brother 扩展到同道、修士与称呼。

definition_en: of the colour of earth, wood or coffee
core_image: 秋天的落叶铺在地上，颜色一层层从浅黄压到深褐
scene: 雨后的土路被人踩过，颜色比旁边的草深了一层。The wet earth looked dark brown after the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 brown 是「棕色」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他穿了一件棕色外套。

derivatives.zh: 由 brown 加 -ish 构成，义为「略带棕色的」
由 brown 加 -ness 构成，义为「棕色」
由 brown 加 -y 构成，义为「偏棕的」

senses.title: The colour of earth or coffee
senses.definition: of the colour of earth, wood or coffee
senses.definitionCN: 泥土、木头或咖啡那种颜色
senses.example: She wore a brown hat.
senses.why: Brown is from Old English brūn, a Germanic colour word for dark earth tones, so the colour is its original sense.
senses.whyCN: brown 来自古英语 brūn，是日耳曼语中表示深土色的词，所以颜色是它最本源的意思。

senses.title: To cook until browned
senses.definition: to make the surface of food brown by heating it
senses.definitionCN: 加热使食物表面变成褐色
senses.example: Brown the meat before adding water.
senses.exampleCN: 加水前先把肉煎至褐色。
senses.why: The verb simply names the result of cooking: heat turns the surface brown, and English often turns a colour into an action that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词直接以结果命名：加热让食物表面变褐，英语常把颜色词变成「使呈现该颜色」的动作。

intro.cn: brown 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Old English brūn meant brown and also dark or shining.
items.cn: 古英语 brūn 既指棕色，也指深色或发亮。

items.en: Germanic *brūnaz is related to the word for bear, an animal of that colour.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *brūnaz 与表示「熊」的词相关，熊正是这种颜色。

items.en: A root meaning 'brown' is reconstructed; its deeper connections are source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般重构出一个表示「棕色」的词根；更深的关联来源不确定。

items.en: Brown settled as a plain colour word for earth, wood and animals.
items.cn: 中古英语时期 brown 固定为指土、木与动物的普通颜色词。

items.en: Brown also names surnames, baked food and tanned skin.
items.cn: 现代英语中 brown 还用于姓氏、烤制食物与晒黑的皮肤。

definition_zh: 公共汽车；巴士；用大巴运送
definition_en: a large road vehicle that carries many passengers for a fare
core_image: 一辆方方正正的公共汽车停在站牌旁，车门一开人就涌进去
scene: 早晨的站牌下排着长队，车一停大家依次上去。The children took the bus to school.
sceneCN: 这里 bus 是「公共汽车」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她在街角赶上了公交。

derivatives.zh: 由 bus 与 stop 复合，义为「公交站」
由 bus 与 driver 复合，义为「公交司机」
由 bus 与 boy 复合，义为「餐馆杂工」

senses.title: A large road vehicle for passengers
senses.definition: a large road vehicle that carries many passengers for a fare
senses.definitionCN: 沿道路行驶、收费运送许多乘客的大型车辆
senses.example: The bus stops outside the school.
senses.exampleCN: 公共汽车停在学校外面。
senses.why: Bus is a short form of omnibus, Latin for for all, because the vehicle carries everyone rather than a private party.
senses.whyCN: bus 是 omnibus 的缩略，拉丁语意为「为所有人」，因为这种车谁都能坐，而不是私人包车。

senses.title: To carry people by bus
senses.definition: to transport people by bus
senses.definitionCN: 用公共汽车运送人员
senses.example: They bused the children to the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用大巴把孩子送到博物馆。
senses.why: English often turns a vehicle noun into a verb, so the bus that carries a group also names the act of carrying them.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把交通工具名词直接当动词，于是运送一群人的 bus 也成了「用大巴运送」这个动作。

intro.en: The history of bus is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: bus 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: The vehicle name comes from French omnibus, 'for all', from Latin omnibus.
items.cn: 这一车名来自法语 omnibus「为所有人」，源自拉丁语 omnibus。

items.en: Omnibus was a shortened name for a carriage that carried everyone.
items.cn: omnibus 原是一种「人人可乘」马车的简称。

items.en: English cut omnibus to bus in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪把 omnibus 缩略为 bus。

items.en: Bus spread to motor vehicles, school transport and computing.
items.cn: bus 扩展到机动车、校车与计算机领域。

items.en: The verb developed from the noun in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 动词用法在二十世纪由名词发展而来。

definition_zh: 再见；顺便一提（bye the way 的口语变体）
definition_en: a short informal word used when leaving someone
core_image: 门口的人抬手挥了一下，转身走下台阶
scene: 校车来了，孩子背上书包，朝门口的母亲挥挥手。Bye, Mum, he called as he ran to the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 bye 是「告别用语」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她挥手说再见。

derivatives.zh: 由 bye 重叠构成的儿语告别语
bye 所由缩略的完整告别语

senses.title: A short word used when leaving
senses.definition: a short informal word said when leaving someone
senses.definitionCN: 离开某人时说的简短告别语
senses.example: She waved bye at the gate.
senses.why: Bye is a worn-down form of goodbye, itself a shortening of God be with ye, so the farewell sense is the everyday one.
senses.whyCN: bye 是 goodbye 磨损后的短形式，而 goodbye 又缩自 God be with ye，所以告别是它日常的用法。

senses.title: A free pass into the next round
senses.definition: the right to go on to the next round without playing
senses.definitionCN: 不必比赛就进入下一轮的权利
senses.example: He got a bye into the second round.
senses.why: This sense comes from by meaning at the side: a player left on the side without an opponent has a bye, not a goodbye.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自表示「在旁边」的 by：被留在旁边、没有对手的选手获得 bye，与告别语 bye 来源不同。

intro.en: The history of bye is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: bye 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Bye is a shortened form of goodbye, recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: bye 是 goodbye 的缩略形式，十六世纪已有记录。

items.en: Goodbye itself comes from 'God be with ye', a blessing at parting.
items.cn: goodbye 本身来自「上帝与你同在」，是告别时的祝福。

items.en: The longer form and its shortened bye coexisted for centuries.
items.cn: 较长形式与缩略形式并存了几个世纪。

items.en: The sporting bye comes from a different line, meaning a free pass.
items.cn: 体育中的「轮空」义来自另一条线索，意为免费通过。

items.en: Bye is now the everyday spoken farewell in English.
items.cn: 现代英语中 bye 是最日常的口头告别语。

definition_zh: 蛋糕；糕点；结成块；轻易完成
definition_en: a sweet baked food made from flour, sugar and eggs
core_image: 刚出炉的圆蛋糕摆在桌上，糖霜还没完全凝住
scene: 生日那天，桌上摆着插了蜡烛的圆点心，孩子们围在旁边。She cut the cake and gave everyone a slice.
sceneCN: 这里 cake 是「甜点蛋糕」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们为她的生日烤了蛋糕。

derivatives.zh: 由 cake 加 -y 构成，义为「像蛋糕的」
由 cup 与 cake 复合，义为「纸杯蛋糕」

senses.title: A sweet baked food
senses.definition: a sweet food baked from flour, sugar, eggs and fat
senses.definitionCN: 用面粉、糖、蛋和油脂烤成的甜食
senses.example: She baked a cake for my birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 她为我的生日烤了一个蛋糕。
senses.why: Cake comes from Old Norse kaka, a flat baked sweet, and the birthday cake is the sense children know first.
senses.whyCN: cake 来自古诺斯语 kaka，指扁平的甜饼，生日蛋糕就是孩子最先认识的意思。

senses.title: A pressed block of something
senses.definition: a small flat block of a solid substance
senses.definitionCN: 压成扁平小块的物质
senses.example: He bought a cake of soap.
senses.why: Soap, wax and mud are pressed into flat blocks shaped like a cake, so the food name was extended to any such block.
senses.whyCN: 肥皂、蜡和泥被压成扁块，形状像蛋糕，于是这个食物名称扩展到任何这样的块状物。

senses.title: To form a hard crust
senses.definition: to become covered with a hard layer, or to form a hard mass
senses.definitionCN: 表面结成硬层，或凝成硬块
senses.example: The mud caked on his boots.
senses.exampleCN: 泥巴在他的靴子上结成了块。
senses.why: When soft material dries into a crust, it looks like the baked top of a cake, which is the picture behind the verb.

items.en: Cake is probably from Old Norse kaka, a flat baked food.
items.cn: cake 可能来自古诺斯语 kaka，一种扁平的烤制食物。

items.en: Germanic *kakǭ is the reconstructed source, also behind German Kuchen.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *kakǭ 是重构来源，也与德语 Kuchen 有关。

items.en: The deeper origin is source uncertain; it may be a loan from outside the family.
items.cn: 更早来源不确定；它可能是来自语族之外的借词。

items.en: Middle English cake covered both flat loaves and sweet baked foods.
items.cn: 中古英语 cake 既指扁平面饼，也指甜烤点。

items.en: The word also gives the hard-mass sense and the idiom piece of cake.
items.cn: 这个词还产生「块状物」义与「轻而易举」的习语。

definition_en: a modal verb expressing ability or possibility, and a metal container
core_image: 一双手把盖子拧开，里面装着能做某事的力气
scene: 厨房的架子上排着一排金属罐，孩子踮脚想拿最上面那个。She can reach the top shelf if she stands on a chair.
sceneCN: 这里 can 是「有能力做」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她游泳游得很好。

collocations.phrase: as far as I can see

senses.title: To be able to do something
senses.definition: to have the ability or skill to do something
senses.definitionCN: 具备做某事的能力或技能
senses.example: I can swim.
senses.why: The modal can goes back to Old English cunnan, to know, because knowing how to do something was the old sense of being able.
senses.whyCN: 情态动词 can 来自古英语 cunnan「知道」，因为「知道怎么做」正是古人对「能够」的理解。

senses.title: To be allowed to do something
senses.definition: to be permitted to do something
senses.definitionCN: 获得许可做某事
senses.example: You can leave now.
senses.why: Permission and ability sit close together: if nothing stops you and you are able, people say you can go.
senses.whyCN: 许可与能力和距离很近：如果没有阻碍、你又做得到，人们就说你可以去。

senses.title: Used to say something is possible
senses.definition: used to say that something is possible
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事有可能发生
senses.example: It can rain here in June.
senses.why: What is possible is what has the power to happen, so can slides from personal ability to events that may occur.
senses.whyCN: 可能发生的事就是「有力量发生」的事，所以 can 从人的能力滑向事件的或然性。

senses.title: A metal container
senses.definition: a metal container for food or drink
senses.definitionCN: 装食物或饮料的金属容器
senses.example: He opened a can of soup.
senses.why: The noun can has a separate origin: Latin canna, a reed or tube, which became the name of a metal cylinder, not the modal verb.
senses.whyCN: 名词 can 来源完全不同：拉丁语 canna 指芦苇或管子，后来成为金属圆罐的名称，与情态动词无关。

definition_en: a road vehicle with an engine that carries a small number of people
core_image: 一辆四个轮子的车停在门口，车门一关就带着人滑出去
scene: 清晨的车库里，父亲把钥匙插进门锁，车灯亮了一下。The family loaded the car and drove out of the city.

senses.title: A road vehicle with an engine
senses.definition: a road vehicle with an engine that carries a small number of people
senses.definitionCN: 载少量人、由发动机驱动的道路车辆
senses.example: He washed his car on Sunday.
senses.why: Car comes from Latin carrus, a wagon, and was first short for motorcar when engines replaced horses.
senses.whyCN: car 来自拉丁语 carrus「四轮车」，发动机取代马匹后，它先作为 motorcar 的简称使用。

senses.title: A railway carriage
senses.definition: one of the separate sections of a train
senses.definitionCN: 列车中供乘客使用的独立车厢
senses.example: We ate in the dining car.
senses.why: A train carriage is a wheeled box that carries people, much like the old wagon, so English keeps car for that section too.
senses.whyCN: 火车车厢是一个载人的带轮箱子，和旧式四轮车很像，所以英语也用 car 指这一节。

items.en: With the motor engine the word shifted to the motor car.

definition_zh: 猫；猫科动物；恶毒的女人（口语）
definition_en: a small furry animal kept as a pet, or any animal of the cat family
core_image: 一只猫伏在窗台上，尾巴慢慢扫过，眼睛盯着外面
scene: 午后的窗台上晒着太阳，毛茸茸的一团把身子摊开。The cat lay on the windowsill and watched the birds.
sceneCN: 这里 cat 是「家猫」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她的猫睡了一整个下午。

collocations.phrase: let the cat out of the bag

derivatives.zh: 由 cat 加 -y 构成，义为「刻薄的」
由 cat 加 -like 构成，义为「猫一样的」
由 cat 与 nap 复合，义为「打盹」

senses.title: A small furry pet animal
senses.definition: a small furry animal often kept as a pet
senses.definitionCN: 常被当作宠物饲养的小型毛茸茸动物
senses.example: The cat slept on the sofa.
senses.why: Cat comes from Old English catt, a word shared across many European languages, and the household pet is its central sense.
senses.whyCN: cat 来自古英语 catt，这个词在欧洲许多语言里都能找到，家猫是它最核心的意思。

senses.title: Any animal of the cat family
senses.definition: a lion, tiger or other large animal of the same family
senses.definitionCN: 狮、虎等与猫同科的大型动物
senses.example: Lions and tigers are big cats.
senses.exampleCN: 狮子和老虎是大型猫科动物。
senses.why: Zoologists group lions and tigers with the house cat, so cat serves as the everyday name for the whole family.
senses.whyCN: 动物学家把狮、虎和家猫归入同一科，于是 cat 成了整个猫科的日常称呼。

intro.en: The history of cat is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: cat 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Old English catt is recorded early, probably from Late Latin cattus.
items.cn: 古英语 catt 早已有记录，可能来自晚期拉丁语 cattus。

items.en: Late Latin cattus spread across Europe with the animal itself.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 cattus 随这种动物一起传遍欧洲。

items.en: The word is often called African or Celtic in origin, but the source is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词常被认为源自非洲或凯尔特语，但来源不确定。

items.en: Middle English cat kept the same form while compounds grew.
items.cn: 中古英语 cat 形式不变，复合词开始增多。

items.en: Cat covers the pet, the family of animals and slang senses.
items.cn: 现代英语中 cat 覆盖宠物、猫科与俚语义。

definition_en: a seat for one person, with a back, or the person who leads a meeting
core_image: 一把有靠背的椅子摆在桌前，等着有人坐下来说话
scene: 会前的屋子很安静，长桌一头摆着一把空着的靠背椅。She took the chair at the head of the table.
sceneCN: 这里 chair 是「单人座椅」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他拉过一把椅子坐下。

derivatives.zh: 由 chair 与 man 复合，义为「主席」
由 chair 与 person 复合，义为「主席（中性）」
由 arm 与 chair 复合，义为「扶手椅」

senses.title: A seat with a back
senses.definition: a seat for one person, usually with a back
senses.definitionCN: 供一人坐、通常带靠背的座位
senses.example: She sat on a wooden chair.
senses.why: Chair came through French from Greek kathedra, a seat, and the furniture sense is the one the word still names first.
senses.whyCN: chair 经法语来自希腊语 kathedra「座位」，家具义项至今仍是它最先指的东西。

senses.title: The person who leads a meeting
senses.definition: the person who leads a meeting or organisation
senses.definitionCN: 主持会议或领导组织的人
senses.example: The chair called the meeting to order.
senses.why: A leader sits in the special chair at the head of the table, so the seat gave its name to the person occupying it.
senses.whyCN: 领导者坐在长桌首位的那把椅子上，于是座位名变成了坐在那里的人的头衔。

senses.title: To lead a meeting or group
senses.definition: to lead a meeting or be in charge of a group
senses.definitionCN: 主持会议或领导一个团体
senses.example: He chaired the committee for a year.
senses.why: From the person in the chair comes the verb: to chair is to do what the chair does, namely lead the discussion.
senses.whyCN: 动词由「坐在椅子上的人」而来：to chair 就是做主席做的事，也就是引导讨论。

intro.en: The history of chair is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: chair 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Chair came through Old French chaiere from Latin cathedra.
items.cn: chair 经由古法语 chaiere 来自拉丁语 cathedra。

items.en: Latin cathedra meant a seat, especially a teacher's seat, from Greek.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cathedra 指座位，尤指教师之座，源自希腊语。

items.en: Greek kathedra was a seat, built from kata 'down' and hedra 'seat'.
items.cn: 希腊语 kathedra 指座位，由 kata「向下」与 hedra「座」构成。

items.en: Middle English chair first meant a throne or seat of authority.
items.cn: 中古英语 chair 最初指宝座或权威之座。

items.en: The everyday furniture sense grew, and the word became a verb.
items.cn: 日常家具义发展起来，这个词又作动词。

definition_en: to shut something, to end, or to be near in space or time
core_image: 两扇门慢慢合拢，最后一道缝也消失了
scene: 傍晚的店里客人渐渐走空，店主走到门口准备收工。She closed the shop and turned off the lights.
sceneCN: 这里 close 是「关闭」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他随手关上了门。

derivatives.zh: 由 close 加 -ed 构成，义为「关闭的」
由 close 加 -ly 构成，义为「紧密地」
由 close 加 -ure 构成，义为「关闭、终止」

senses.title: To shut something
senses.definition: to shut a door, window or lid
senses.definitionCN: 把门、窗或盖子合上
senses.example: Please close the window.
senses.why: The verb close comes from Latin claudere, to shut, and the physical act of shutting is its oldest use.
senses.whyCN: 动词 close 来自拉丁语 claudere「关闭」，把东西合上这个具体动作是最早的用法。

senses.title: To bring something to an end
senses.definition: to end an activity, meeting or period
senses.definitionCN: 使活动、会议或时期结束
senses.example: The shop will close at six.
senses.why: Shutting a building or a meeting is like shutting a lid: activity stops, so close also means to end.
senses.whyCN: 关上一栋楼或一场会议就像盖上盖子：活动停止，所以 close 也表示「结束」。

senses.title: Near in space or time
senses.definition: near in distance or time
senses.definitionCN: 距离或时间上接近
senses.example: We live close to the school.
senses.why: This adjective is pronounced with a soft s and comes from French clos, enclosed, meaning places packed near one another.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词读作清音 s，来自法语 clos「围起来的」，指彼此挨得很近的地方。

senses.title: Near in relationship
senses.definition: having a strong personal bond
senses.definitionCN: 有深厚私人感情的
senses.example: We are close friends.
senses.why: People who live close become emotionally close, so the distance word extends to relationships.
senses.whyCN: 住得近的人感情也会近，于是表示距离的词扩展到了关系上。

intro.en: The history of close is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: close 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Latin claudere meant 'to shut, to close off'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 claudere 意为「关闭、围合」。

items.en: Old French clore, with stem clos-, carried the verb into English.
items.cn: 古法语 clore（词干 clos-）把这一动词带入英语。

items.en: Close entered English as a verb and later produced closed and closure.
items.cn: close 以动词身份进入英语，后来产生 closed 与 closure。

items.en: The adjective close, 'near', developed from the same shut-in idea.
items.cn: 形容词 close「近」由同一个「围合」的想法发展而来。

items.en: Two pronunciations now separate the verb from the adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语用两种读音区分动词与形容词。

definition_en: of a low temperature, unfriendly in manner, or a common illness
core_image: 雪后的窗玻璃上结着一层白霜，手指一碰就缩回来
scene: 清晨的院子里，水桶边缘结了一圈薄冰。The morning was cold, so they lit the stove early.
sceneCN: 这里 cold 是「温度低」（第 01 个义项）；句意是水太冷了，不能游泳。

derivatives.zh: 由 cold 加 -ly 构成，义为「冷淡地」
由 cold 加 -ness 构成，义为「寒冷、冷淡」
由 cold 与 blooded 复合，义为「冷血的」

senses.title: Of low temperature
senses.definition: having a low temperature
senses.definitionCN: 温度低的
senses.example: The water is cold.
senses.why: Cold is a native Germanic word for low temperature, and the weather sense is the one everyone learns first.
senses.whyCN: cold 是日耳曼语本族词，表示低温，天气寒冷是所有人最先学会的意思。

senses.title: Unfriendly in manner
senses.definition: showing no warmth or friendliness
senses.definitionCN: 态度上不热情、不友好
senses.example: He gave me a cold look.
senses.why: A person without friendliness feels as uninviting as cold air, so the temperature word describes social distance.
senses.whyCN: 缺乏友善的人像冷空气一样让人不敢靠近，于是温度词被用来形容人际距离。

senses.title: A common illness of the nose and throat
senses.definition: a mild illness with sneezing and a sore throat
senses.definitionCN: 打喷嚏、喉咙痛的轻微疾病
senses.example: She caught a cold last week.
senses.why: Old medicine linked such illness to exposure to cold air, and the name of the cause became the name of the sickness.
senses.whyCN: 旧时的医学把这类病归因于受寒，于是病因的名称变成了病名。

items.cn: 日耳曼语 *kaldaz 是重构来源，与德语 kalt 相关。

items.en: A root *gel- 'cold' is reconstructed and also lies behind glacier and gelid.
items.cn: 词根 *gel-「冷」被重构，glacier 与 gelid 也出自此根。

items.en: The spelling settled as cold while the illness sense developed.
items.cn: 中古英语时期拼写固定为 cold，疾病义同时发展。

items.en: Cold covers temperature, manner, illness and unreadiness.
items.cn: 现代英语中 cold 覆盖温度、态度、疾病与无准备。

definition_en: to move toward a place or person, or to reach a state
core_image: 一条路从远处收拢到脚下，脚步一步步把距离缩短
scene: 院门开着，脚步声从巷口一直传到屋里。Come inside before the rain starts.
sceneCN: 这里 come 是「来到说话人这里」（第 01 个义项）；句意是过来坐我旁边。

derivatives.zh: 由 come 加 -ing 构成，义为「即将到来的」
由 come 加 -er 构成，义为「来者」
由 out 与 come 复合，义为「结果」

senses.title: To move toward the speaker
senses.definition: to move toward the place where the speaker is
senses.definitionCN: 朝说话人所在的地方移动
senses.example: Please come to my party.
senses.why: Come is an old Germanic verb for moving nearer, and its centre is motion toward the person speaking.
senses.whyCN: come 是古老的日耳曼语动词，表示向近处移动，核心就是朝说话人靠近。

senses.title: To arrive or appear
senses.definition: to arrive at a place, or to appear in time
senses.definitionCN: 抵达某处，或随时间出现
senses.example: The letter came this morning.
senses.why: Once the movement is finished, the verb reports the arrival, so a letter or a season can come without anyone walking.
senses.whyCN: 移动一旦完成，动词就报告「到达」，所以信或季节也能 come，即使没有人在走路。

senses.title: To reach a new state
senses.definition: to pass into a particular state or condition
senses.definitionCN: 进入某种状态或情形
senses.example: Her dream came true.
senses.why: Moving toward a place resembles moving toward a condition, so come true means reach the state of being true.
senses.whyCN: 朝一个地方移动类似于朝一种状态移动，所以 come true 就是抵达「成真」的状态。

senses.title: To have a particular origin
senses.definition: to originate from a place, person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 源自某个地方、人或事物
senses.example: She comes from a small town.
senses.why: Where someone starts and then moves from is their origin, so come from answers the question of source.
senses.whyCN: 一个人出发并离开的地方就是来源，所以 come from 回答的是「从哪里来」。

items.cn: come 来自古英语 cuman，意为「移动、到达」。

items.cn: 日耳曼语 *kwemaną 也衍生出德语 kommen 与荷兰语 komen。

items.cn: *ɡʷem-「迈步、走」被重构为这个词根。

items.en: The past came and the participle come took their modern shapes.
items.cn: 中古英语时期过去式 came 与过去分词 come 定型。

items.en: Come extends from movement to origin, order and resulting states.
items.cn: 现代英语中 come 从移动扩展到来源、顺序与结果状态。

definition_en: an informal word for father
core_image: 一个男人把孩子扛在肩上，走过傍晚的街口
scene: 傍晚的巷口，一个男人弯腰把孩子抱起来，孩子笑出声。Dad lifted the boy onto his shoulders.
sceneCN: 这里 dad 是「爸爸」（第 01 个义项）；句意是爸爸今晚给我读了个故事。

derivatives.zh: 由 dad 加 -y 构成的儿语称呼，义为「爸爸」
由 dad 与 joke 复合，义为「老爸式冷笑话」

senses.title: A father, used when speaking to him
senses.definition: father, used as a form of address
senses.definitionCN: 当面称呼父亲时使用的口语词
senses.example: Dad, can I go out?
senses.why: Dad is a nursery word built from the first sounds a baby makes, so it began as the name a child calls a father face to face.
senses.whyCN: dad 是幼儿最容易发出的音节构成的儿语词，最初就是孩子当面叫父亲时用的称呼。

senses.title: A father, used when talking about him
senses.definition: father, used when telling someone about him
senses.definitionCN: 向别人叙述时指称自己的父亲
senses.example: My dad works at a bank.
senses.why: The same word also appears in my dad, where the child is not calling but telling a third person who the father is.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也出现在 my dad 里，这时孩子不是当面呼唤，而是告诉第三者父亲是谁。

intro.en: The history of dad is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: dad 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Dad belongs to the nursery words that babies produce easily, like papa.
items.cn: dad 属于婴儿容易发出的儿语词，与 papa 同类。

items.en: The word is recorded in English from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词自十六世纪起在英语中有记录。

items.en: Similar forms appear in many languages without proof of one common source.
items.cn: 许多语言有相似形式，但没有证据表明出自同一来源。

items.en: Dad became the everyday spoken word for father in English.
items.cn: 现代英语中 dad 成为口语里日常使用的「爸爸」。

items.en: In some regions it also serves as a friendly address to older men.
items.cn: 在一些地区，它也用作对年长男子的亲切称呼。

definition_zh: 跳舞；舞蹈；舞会；随着音乐摆动
definition_en: to move the body rhythmically, usually to music
core_image: 裙摆随鼓点转开，脚尖在地上点出一圈圈节奏
scene: 院子里的收音机响起来，孩子们跟着节拍转圈。The children began to dance when the music started.
sceneCN: 这里 dance 是「跳舞」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他们跳到半夜。

derivatives.zh: 由 dance 加 -er 构成，义为「舞者」
由 dance 加 -ing 构成，义为「跳舞」
由 dance 与 floor 复合，义为「舞池」

senses.title: To move the body to music
senses.definition: to move the body rhythmically, usually to music
senses.definitionCN: 通常合着音乐有节奏地摆动身体
senses.example: They dance in the school hall.
senses.why: Dance entered English from Old French dancier, to move in a lively way, and the action of moving to music is its core sense.
senses.whyCN: dance 从古法语 dancier「活泼地移动」进入英语，合着音乐舞动是它最核心的意思。

senses.title: A particular set of dance steps
senses.definition: a style or piece of dancing with fixed steps
senses.definitionCN: 有固定动作的一套舞蹈
senses.example: She learned a new dance.
senses.why: Once steps are fixed and repeated, the action becomes a named thing, so people speak of a dance rather than only dancing.
senses.whyCN: 动作一旦固定并反复出现，行为就变成有名有姓的事物，于是人们说 a dance，而不只是 dancing。

senses.title: A social event with dancing
senses.definition: a party where people dance
senses.definitionCN: 人们跳舞的社交聚会
senses.example: We went to the school dance.
senses.why: A gathering organised around dancing took the name of the activity itself, as English often does with events.
senses.whyCN: 以跳舞为中心的聚会直接借用了活动本身的名字，英语常用这种方式命名活动。

intro.cn: dance 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Dance came from Old French dancier, first recorded in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: dance 来自古法语 dancier，十三世纪已有记录。

items.en: The French verb is often traced to a Frankish word meaning to move or tremble; the source is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个法语动词常被追溯到法兰克语中表示「移动、颤动」的词；来源不确定。

items.en: Middle English dance covered both the action and the social event.
items.cn: 中古英语 dance 既指动作，也指社交舞会。

items.en: Dance extends to art, music and any rhythmic movement.
items.cn: 现代英语中 dance 扩展到艺术、音乐与任何有节奏的运动。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as dance floor and dance music keep the word active.
items.cn: dance floor、dance music 等固定短语让这个词保持活跃。

senses.title: A table for writing or working
senses.definition: a table with a flat top used for writing or working
senses.definitionCN: 供书写或工作的平面桌子
senses.example: She sat at her desk and wrote.
senses.why: Desk came through Italian and Latin from Greek diskos, a flat round plate, and it still names a flat working surface.
senses.whyCN: desk 经意大利语和拉丁语来自希腊语 diskos「扁平圆盘」，至今仍指扁平的工作台面。

senses.title: A counter where staff serve people
senses.definition: a counter in a hotel, office or shop where staff help visitors
senses.definitionCN: 旅馆、办公室或商店里接待来客的柜台
senses.example: Please ask at the front desk.
senses.why: Hotel and office counters are built like high desks, so the furniture word became the name of the service point.
senses.whyCN: 旅馆和办公室的柜台做得像高书桌，于是家具词变成了服务点的名称。

intro.en: The history of desk is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: desk 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Desk goes back to Latin discus, a disc or table, through Italian desco.
items.cn: desk 可追溯到拉丁语 discus「圆盘、桌面」，经意大利语 desco。

items.en: Medieval Latin desca named a table for writing or counting.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 desca 指写字或计数的桌子。

items.en: English borrowed the word as desk, a reading or writing table.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入该词，指读写用的桌子。

items.en: Desk extends to office furniture and service counters.
items.cn: 现代英语中 desk 扩展到办公家具与服务台。

items.en: News desks and front desks name the people working at them.
items.cn: 新闻编辑台与前台以桌子代指在那里工作的人。

definition_en: a domesticated animal kept as a pet or for work
core_image: 一只狗守在门口，耳朵竖着，听到脚步就抬头
scene: 院子门口趴着一只黄狗，谁来都要先让它闻一闻。The dog ran to the gate when it heard the bell.
sceneCN: 这里 dog 是「家犬」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他们的狗睡在炉边。

derivatives.zh: 由 dog 加 -y 构成的儿语称呼，义为「狗狗」
由 dog 加 -ed 构成，义为「顽强的」
由 dog 与 house 复合，义为「狗屋」

senses.title: A domesticated animal kept as a pet
senses.definition: a domesticated animal kept as a pet or for work
senses.definitionCN: 被当作宠物饲养或用于工作的家养动物
senses.example: The dog ran across the field.
senses.why: Dog comes from Old English docga, a word of unclear origin that replaced the older hound for the household animal.
senses.whyCN: dog 来自古英语 docga，来源不明，它取代了更早的 hound，成为这种家养动物的常用称呼。

senses.title: To follow someone persistently
senses.definition: to follow someone closely and persistently
senses.definitionCN: 紧跟某人、不断纠缠
senses.example: Reporters dogged him for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们跟踪纠缠了他几个星期。
senses.why: A dog that follows a scent or a person never gives up, so the animal name became a verb for relentless following.
senses.whyCN: 狗循着气味或跟着人时从不轻易放弃，于是动物名变成了表示「紧追不舍」的动词。

senses.title: A person, in a friendly or joking tone
senses.definition: a person, used in a familiar or joking way
senses.definitionCN: 口语中带亲昵或戏谑地指一个人
senses.example: He is a lucky dog.
senses.why: Old informal speech used dog for a fellow, much as friends today call someone a lucky dog without insulting him.
senses.whyCN: 旧时口语用 dog 指「家伙」，就像今天朋友说 lucky dog，并没有骂人的意思。

items.cn: 这个词没有清楚的日耳曼同族词，可能是较晚的英语造词。

items.en: Dog gradually replaced the older word hund in everyday use.
items.cn: dog 在日常用语中逐渐取代较早的 hund。

items.en: Middle English dog extended to working animals and slang.
items.cn: 中古英语 dog 扩展到工作犬与俚语。

items.en: The verb sense of following or troubling someone grew later.

definition_en: a movable panel that opens and closes an entrance
core_image: 一块木板装在门框上，推开就看见里面的一整个房间
scene: 楼道尽头的那扇木门半掩着，里面透出一条灯光。He knocked twice and the door opened.
sceneCN: 这里 door 是「门」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她夜里锁上门。

derivatives.zh: 由 door 加 -way 构成，义为「门口」
由 door 与 knob 复合，义为「门把手」
由 out 与 door 复合，义为「户外的」

senses.title: A panel that opens an entrance
senses.definition: a movable panel that opens and closes an entrance
senses.definitionCN: 可以开合、用于进出的一道板状物
senses.example: Please close the door.
senses.why: Door comes from Old English duru, the Germanic word for the opening of a house, and the panel sense grew from it.
senses.whyCN: door 来自古英语 duru，是日耳曼语中表示房屋开口的词，能开合的门板义项由此发展而来。

senses.title: The entrance or doorway itself
senses.definition: the opening or space where you enter
senses.definitionCN: 供人进出的开口或位置
senses.example: Someone is standing at the door.
senses.why: People say at the door when they mean the opening rather than the panel, so the word names both the thing and the space.
senses.whyCN: 人们说 at the door 时指的是开口而不是门板，所以这个词既指门板也指门口的空间。

senses.title: A way to reach an opportunity
senses.definition: a means of reaching an opportunity or a new situation
senses.definitionCN: 通向机会或新境况的途径
senses.example: Education opens doors for young people.
senses.exampleCN: 教育为年轻人打开机会之门。
senses.why: A real door lets you into a room, and English uses the same picture for anything that lets you into a new opportunity.
senses.whyCN: 真实的门让人进入房间，英语用同一幅画面比喻任何能让人进入新机会的东西。

items.en: Germanic *durz is behind German Tür and Dutch deur.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *durz 也衍生出德语 Tür 与荷兰语 deur。

items.en: *dʰwer- 'door, gateway' is reconstructed as the root.

items.en: The forms merged into the modern door.

items.en: Door extends to vehicles, furniture and figurative openings.
items.cn: 现代英语中 door 扩展到车辆、家具与比喻性的开口。

definition_en: to take liquid into the mouth and swallow it, or liquid for drinking
core_image: 一只杯子举到嘴边，水线一点点降下去
scene: 跑完操场的孩子满头是汗，抓起水壶一口气灌下去。He drank the whole bottle of water after the race.
sceneCN: 这里 drink 是「喝」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她喝了一杯牛奶。

derivatives.zh: 由 drink 加 -er 构成，义为「饮酒者」
由 drink 加 -ing 构成，义为「饮用」
由 drink 加 -able 构成，义为「可饮用的」

senses.title: To take liquid into the mouth
senses.definition: to take liquid into the mouth and swallow it
senses.definitionCN: 把液体送入口中并咽下
senses.example: I drink water every morning.
senses.why: Drink is an old Germanic verb for swallowing liquid, and that physical action is its central sense.
senses.whyCN: drink 是古老的日耳曼语动词，表示咽下液体，这个具体动作是它最核心的意思。

senses.title: Liquid for drinking
senses.definition: a liquid that people drink
senses.definitionCN: 供人饮用的液体
senses.example: Milk is a healthy drink.
senses.why: English often uses the same form for an action and its object, so the act of drinking also names what is drunk.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用同一个形式表示动作和对象，所以「喝」这个动作也指被喝的东西。

senses.title: To consume alcohol
senses.definition: to take alcoholic drinks
senses.definitionCN: 饮用含酒精的饮料
senses.example: He does not drink at parties.
senses.why: Because alcohol is the drink most often singled out in social rules, the bare verb drink can mean to use alcohol.
senses.whyCN: 因为在社交规范里最常被单独提起的饮品是酒，所以光用动词 drink 就能表示「喝酒」。

intro.en: The history of drink is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: drink 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Drink comes from Old English drincan, 'to swallow liquid'.
items.cn: drink 来自古英语 drincan，意为「吞下液体」。

items.en: Germanic *drinkaną is behind German trinken and Dutch drinken.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *drinkaną 也衍生出德语 trinken 与荷兰语 drinken。

items.en: *dʰreǵ- 'to draw, drink' is reconstructed as the root.
items.cn: *dʰreǵ-「拉、饮」被重构为词根。

items.en: Middle English drink served both verb and noun.
items.cn: 中古英语 drink 兼作动词与名词。

items.en: Drink covers water, alcohol and figurative absorption.
items.cn: 现代英语中 drink 覆盖水、酒与比喻性的吸收。

definition_en: a water bird with a flat bill, or to lower the head quickly
core_image: 一只鸭子贴着水面滑过去，头一低就钻进水里
scene: 池塘边的芦苇晃了一下，一只扁嘴的鸟低头钻进水里。The duck dived under the water when it saw us.
sceneCN: 这里 duck 是「鸭子」（第 01 个义项）；句意是一只鸭子游过池塘。

derivatives.zh: 由 duck 加指小后缀 -ling 构成，义为「小鸭」
由 duck 加 -y 构成，义为「可爱的」（口语）

senses.title: A water bird with a flat bill
senses.definition: a water bird with a flat bill and webbed feet
senses.definitionCN: 有扁平嘴和蹼足的水鸟
senses.example: The duck swam across the pond.
senses.why: Duck comes from Old English dūce, the female of the water bird, and it became the everyday name for the whole kind.
senses.whyCN: duck 来自古英语 dūce，原本指这种水鸟的雌鸟，后来成为整个种类的日常称呼。

senses.title: The meat of a duck
senses.definition: duck eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物的鸭肉
senses.example: We had roast duck for dinner.
senses.why: Meat names often repeat the animal name in English, so a duck on a menu is the bird served as food.
senses.whyCN: 英语里肉类常沿用动物名，所以菜单上的 duck 就是作为食物端上桌的鸭子。

senses.title: To lower your head quickly
senses.definition: to move your head down quickly to avoid something
senses.definitionCN: 迅速低头以避开某物
senses.example: She ducked under the low branch.
senses.exampleCN: 她低头从低矮的树枝下钻过。
senses.why: This verb does not come from the bird: it goes back to Old English dūcan, to dive, and describes the same quick downward movement.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词并非来自鸭子：它可追溯到古英语 dūcan「潜水」，描述的是同样的快速下潜动作。

intro.en: The history of duck is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: duck 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: The bird name comes from Old English duce, from dūcan 'to dive'.
items.cn: 鸟名来自古英语 duce，出自 dūcan「潜水」。

items.en: Germanic *dūkaną 'to dive, bend down' also gives the modern verb duck.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *dūkaną「潜水、俯身」也产生现代动词 duck。

items.en: Middle English duck named the bird; the verb kept the diving motion.
items.cn: 中古英语 duck 指这种鸟，动词则保留「下潜」的动作。

items.en: The verb widened to dodging and avoiding.
items.cn: 现代英语中动词扩展到躲闪与回避。

items.en: Duck also names the meat and a British term of endearment.
items.cn: duck 还指鸭肉，并作英式亲昵称呼。

definition_en: the organ of hearing, or the ability to hear sounds
core_image: 侧脸贴着一只耳朵，连最轻的风声都能收进去
scene: 雨点打在瓦上，孩子侧过头，把一边耳朵贴近窗缝。She pressed her ear to the window to hear the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 ear 是「耳朵」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他仔细清洗耳朵。

senses.title: The organ of hearing
senses.definition: the organ on each side of the head used for hearing
senses.definitionCN: 头部两侧用来听声音的器官
senses.example: He covered his ear when the bell rang.
senses.why: Ear comes from Old English ēare, the Germanic name for the hearing organ, and the body part is its first sense.
senses.whyCN: ear 来自古英语 ēare，是日耳曼语中表示听觉器官的词，身体部位是它最早的意思。

senses.title: The ability to hear and judge sound
senses.definition: the ability to hear sounds well, especially music
senses.definitionCN: 分辨声音的能力，尤指对音乐的敏感
senses.example: She has a good ear for music.
senses.exampleCN: 她对音乐有很好的感受力。
senses.why: The organ that receives sound stands for the skill of judging it, so a good ear means good hearing or musical taste.
senses.whyCN: 接收声音的器官代指判断声音的能力，所以 a good ear 指听力好或乐感好。

senses.title: A seed-bearing head of grain
senses.definition: the part of a cereal plant that holds the grains
senses.definitionCN: 谷类植物结籽的穗状部分
senses.example: The farmer picked an ear of corn.
senses.why: This ear has a separate origin: Old English ēar meant a grain spike, and it only shares the spelling with the hearing organ.
senses.whyCN: 这个 ear 来源不同：古英语 ēar 指谷穗，它与表示耳朵的词只是拼写相同。

definition_en: to put food into the mouth, chew and swallow it
core_image: 一碗热饭摆在面前，筷子一夹，碗底慢慢露出来
scene: 干完活的晌午，一家人围坐，碗里的饭冒着热气。The family ate together at the kitchen table.
sceneCN: 这里 eat 是「吃东西」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她上课前吃了一个梨。

senses.title: To put food in the mouth and swallow
senses.definition: to put food into the mouth, chew it and swallow it
senses.definitionCN: 把食物送入口中、咀嚼并咽下
senses.example: We eat breakfast at seven.
senses.why: Eat comes from Old English etan, the old Germanic verb for taking food, and that everyday action is its central sense.
senses.whyCN: eat 来自古英语 etan，是日耳曼语中表示进食的旧动词，这个日常动作是它最核心的意思。

senses.title: To wear away or use up something
senses.definition: to wear away or use up something gradually
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐磨损或耗尽某物
senses.example: The acid ate through the metal.
senses.why: Acid and costs consume material the way a mouth consumes food, so eat extends to anything that wears something away.
senses.whyCN: 酸液和开销像嘴吃食物一样消耗材料，所以 eat 扩展到任何逐渐磨掉东西的过程。

definition_en: the oval object laid by a female bird, used as food

senses.title: The oval object laid by a bird
senses.definition: the oval object laid by a female bird, eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 雌鸟产下的椭圆形物体，可作食物
senses.example: She boiled an egg for breakfast.
senses.why: Egg comes from Old Norse egg, which replaced the older English word and became the name of the bird's oval shell.
senses.whyCN: egg 来自古诺斯语 egg，取代了英语中更早的词，成为鸟类椭圆形外壳产物的名称。

senses.title: A female reproductive cell

senses.example: Each egg holds one cell.

senses.why: The bird's egg is a single large cell, so biology borrowed the everyday word for the reproductive cell of many animals.

root: 借自古诺斯语 egg，取代本族词 ey；来自日耳曼语 *ajją，更早的印欧词根一般重构为 *h₂ōwyóm。

sensesIntro.en: Egg is the bird's shelled product and, in biology, the female reproductive cell.
sensesIntro.cn: egg 指鸟类产下的带壳蛋，在生物学上也指雌性生殖细胞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an oval egg on the counter, a wisp of straw still on the shell
core.cn: 核心意象：一只椭圆的白蛋摆在灶台边，壳上还带着一点草屑

branches.en: FOOD: a boiled egg on the plate.
branches.cn: 食物线：盘里的煮鸡蛋。

branches.en: BIRD: a hen sitting on her eggs.
branches.cn: 鸟类线：母鸡孵蛋。

branches.en: SHAPE: an egg-shaped stone.
branches.cn: 形状线：蛋形的石头。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: a frog's egg in the water.
branches.cn: 生物线：水里的蛙卵。

branches.en: CELL: one egg, one cell.
branches.cn: 细胞线：一个卵就是一个细胞。

intro.en: The word is broken into its base and the ordinary English endings it takes.
intro.cn: 这个词可以拆成主词与它所用的普通英语词尾。
